skill.name: html-injection-testing
skill.description: Guide authorized testers through identifying, validating, documenting, and remediating HTML injection vulnerabilities in web applications.
skill.summary: Test authorized web applications for HTML injection and document impact, evidence, and remediation.
skill.author: zebbern

security_audit.summary: The script and shell alerts are false positives caused by fenced examples and defensive snippets. The documented requests, external resources, and encoding bypass create real network, evasion, and data-capture risks. The skill provides critical phishing guidance plus high-risk defacement, tracking, filter-evasion, and automated probing despite its authorized-use notice.

remediation.issue: Credential-capture examples submit data to public-looking external domains.
remediation.suggestion: Replace them with non-submitting local mock forms and reserved .invalid destinations. Remove instructions that capture usernames, passwords, or cookies.

remediation.issue: The skill provides stealth tracking, defacement, redirect, and filter-evasion payloads.
remediation.suggestion: Limit examples to harmless visual markers. Reframe bypass material as defensive detection guidance and remove covert tracking or phishing behavior.

remediation.issue: Active curl and Python probes lack technical target controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit target confirmation, an allowlist, rate limits, and stop conditions before any request. Default examples to localhost or isolated fixtures.

content.user_title: Test Web Applications for HTML Injection
content.value_statement: Unsanitized input can alter pages, mislead users, and expose credentials. This skill guides authorized HTML injection testing, impact assessment, and remediation reporting.
actual_capabilities: Maps common reflected, stored, path, form, cookie, and header injection surfaces.
Provides test payload categories for formatting, links, images, forms, styles, redirects, and iframes.
Explains manual testing with browsers, proxies, curl, Burp Suite, and OWASP ZAP.
Includes a Python example for sending encoded payloads and checking response reflection.
Distinguishes HTML injection from XSS and assesses phishing, defacement, and reputation impact.
Shows remediation patterns for PHP, Python, JavaScript, output encoding, validation, CSP, and WAF rules.
limitations: It cannot verify target ownership or authorization before tests run.
Several examples can send requests, alter stored content, or display deceptive forms.
Reflection checks do not prove browser rendering, exploitability, or absence of XSS.
Browser sanitization, CSP, WAF rules, and application context can change results.

use_cases.title: Validate a Staging Application
use_cases.description: Check authorized inputs for reflected or stored HTML rendering and document reproducible evidence.

use_cases.title: Review Output Handling
use_cases.description: Compare vulnerable rendering paths with contextual encoding and sanitization controls.

use_cases.title: Build Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Turn confirmed injection cases into controlled security tests with harmless markers.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Reflection Check
prompt_templates.prompt: Review parameter [name] on this authorized staging URL for reflected HTML injection. Use harmless formatting tags and report evidence without changing stored data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner validation of one reflected parameter

prompt_templates.title: Stored Input Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess [profile field] in the authorized test account for stored HTML injection. Use a visible marker, record persistence, and avoid credential forms.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate testing of stored user content

prompt_templates.title: Impact and Remediation Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the confirmed HTML injection at [location]. Explain realistic impact, distinguish it from XSS, and propose contextual output encoding and validation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of a confirmed finding

prompt_templates.title: Controlled Coverage Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an authorized HTML injection test plan for [application]. Cover reflected, stored, path, header, and encoding contexts with rate limits and stop conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning across multiple input surfaces

output_examples.input: Assess the search parameter on our authorized staging site using harmless payloads.
output: Result: A heading marker rendered in the response and changed page structure.
Classification: Reflected HTML injection; no script execution was observed.
Recommendation: Apply contextual output encoding and add a regression test.

output_examples.input: Review a profile biography field for stored HTML injection.
output: Result: The marker persisted and appeared for another authorized test account.
Impact: Stored content can mislead users and alter trusted page elements.
Recommendation: Sanitize permitted markup and encode all other content during rendering.

output_examples.input: Explain how to fix a confirmed unsafe browser rendering path.
output_examples.output: Use text rendering for plain content. When markup is required, apply an allowlist sanitizer and verify the result with regression tests.

best_practices: Obtain written authorization and define target scope, rate limits, and stop conditions before testing.
Begin with harmless visual markers and escalate impact validation only when the assessment requires it.
Record the request, response, browser behavior, context, persistence, and remediation evidence for every confirmed finding.
anti_patterns: Do not test public systems, production users, or third-party domains without explicit authorization.
Do not collect credentials, cookies, personal data, or session tokens during proof-of-concept testing.
Do not classify simple reflection as exploitable until browser rendering and output context are verified.

faq.question: How is HTML injection different from XSS?
faq.answer: HTML injection changes rendered markup. XSS executes script, although unsafe HTML contexts can sometimes lead to XSS.

faq.question: Does reflected input prove a vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. Confirm that the browser interprets input as markup and that contextual encoding does not neutralize it.

faq.question: Can this skill test production systems?
faq.answer: Only with explicit written authorization, defined scope, approved payloads, rate limits, and rollback procedures.

faq.question: Which payload should a test begin with?
faq.answer: Use a harmless formatting marker that makes no network request and collects no data.

faq.question: What evidence should a report include?
faq.answer: Include the input location, sanitized request details, response behavior, browser result, persistence, impact, and recommended fix.

faq.question: How should developers remediate HTML injection?
faq.answer: Use contextual output encoding by default. When markup is required, sanitize with a maintained allowlist library and test every rendering context.
